Which country is Yakovlev MC-21 based from?
Yakovlev MC-21: Russia. The aircraft made its maiden flight on 28 May 2017 from Irkutsk.
Who is credited with discovering Livermorium?
Livermorium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Livermorium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lv and atomic number 116.
Who is credited with discovering Fentanyl?
Fentanyl: Paul Janssen. Fentanyl is a highly potent synthetic opioid of the piperidine family, used primarily as pain medication.
Who is credited with discovering Arsenic?
Arsenic: Albertus Magnus. Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.
An economist who once worked for the IMF and later served as Prime Minister of Côte d'Ivoire from 1990 to 1993, this politician has been the country's president since 2010 — name this leader?
Alassane Ouattara (French; born 1 January 1942) is an Ivorian politician and economist who has been President of Ivory Coast (Cte d'Ivoire) since 2010.
Whether from too few red blood cells or faulty hemoglobin, this disorder leaves the blood less able to carry oxygen — often felt as quiet tiredness long before any paleness shows — what is it?
Anemia (also spelt anaemia in British English) is a blood disorder in which the blood has a reduced ability to carry oxygen.
Sharing chemistry with phosphorus and antimony, this group-15 metalloid carries the symbol As and a notorious reputation for toxicity — what is it?
Arsenic is a chemical element; it has the symbol As and atomic number 33.

This genus of deciduous trees includes 14 species across two subgenera, one found only in East Asia with low, multi-trunked growth, the other spanning Europe, Asia, and eastern North America. What tree genus is this?

Beech (genus Fagus) is a genus of deciduous trees in the family Fagaceae, native to subtropical (accessory forest element) and temperate (as dominant element of mesophytic forests) Eurasia and North America.
As Square's chief technology officer, this software engineer helped build Cash App before he was fatally stabbed in San Francisco in 2023 — who was he?
Bob Lee (businessman) (December 20, 1979 - April 4, 2023) was an American businessman and software engineer who was best known for helping to create the financial service Cash App.
Located between the lower back and the perineum, these two rounded regions of human anatomy are built around the gluteus maximus — the largest muscle in the human body — name this body part?
Buttocks (sing.: buttock) are two rounded portions of the exterior anatomy of humans, located on the posterior of the pelvic region.
Portuguese explorers carried this tropical American tree to India in the 16th century; today Ivory Coast and India lead a 3.9-million-ton global harvest of its nut — what is it?
Cashew is the common name of a tropical evergreen tree Anacardium occidentale, in the family Anacardiaceae.
The first element in group 6, it lends its name to the shiny plating on car bumpers and, mixed into steel, makes it stainless. Which steely-grey metal is it?
Chromium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cr and atomic number 24.
This bird's name comes from the Quechua word 'kuntur,' and its California-dwelling relative was nearly wiped out by habitat loss — which giant vulture soars over the Andes?
Condor is the common name for two genera of New World vultures, each with one extant species.
As of December 2025 worth an estimated $8.7 billion, this Swedish businessman founded and chairs a massive music-streaming company — who is he?
Daniel Ek (Swedish; born 21 February 1983) is a Swedish businessman and technologist.
Found in nighttime cold remedies like NyQuil and paired with vitamin B6 for pregnancy-related nausea, this antihistamine is an inverse agonist at the H1 receptor — which drug?
Doxylamine is an antihistamine medication used to treat insomnia and allergies, and - in combination with pyridoxine (vitamin B6) - to treat morning sickness in pregnant women.
This inner lining of the uterus thickens each cycle and is shed during menstruation in humans and a handful of other species, including certain bats and shrews — what is it?
Endometrium is the inner lining of the uterus (womb) in mammals.
Cats in this subfamily can purr but never roar, thanks to a bony rather than flexible hyoid bone — which subfamily?
Felinae are a subfamily of the Felidae distinguished by a bony hyoid, because of which they can purr but not roar.

A French economist who gave lectures up and down the country and helped found the Inter-Parliamentary Union, he shared the very first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901 for his work in Europe's peace movement — who was he?
Frédéric Passy (20 May 1822 - 12 June 1912) was a French economist and pacifist who was a founding member of several peace societies and the Inter-Parliamentary Union.
This week-long 2010 manhunt across Tyne and Wear and Northumberland ended when the fugitive shot himself following a six-hour standoff near Rothbury. What event is it?
Goose (pl.: geese) is a bird of any of several waterfowl species in the family Anatidae.

Linked to conditions like tuberculosis, bronchitis, and lung cancer, this medical term describes blood discharged from the airway rather than internal bleeding elsewhere in the body. What is it called?
Hemoptysis is the discharge of blood or blood-stained mucus through the mouth coming from the bronchi, larynx, trachea, or lungs.
This negatively charged ion, one oxygen bonded to one hydrogen, acts as a base and forms industrially vital salts like the sodium version used to make millions of tons of chemicals. What ion is it?
Hydroxide (occasionally hydroxyl ion) is a diatomic anion with chemical formula OH.
One of the largest dog breeds in the world, this sighthound was historically used to course game and became the official mascot of a British Guards regiment in 1902. What breed is it?
Irish Wolfhound is a breed of large sighthound that has, by its presence and substantial size, inspired literature, poetry and mythology.
This Johns Hopkins psychologist coined the terms 'gender role' and 'sexual orientation' and believed gender was malleable during a child's first two years. Who was he?
John Money (8 July 1921 - 7 July 2006) was a New Zealand American psychologist, sexologist and professor at Johns Hopkins University known for his research on human sexual behavior and gender.
These paired folds of skin are the major externally visible structures of the vulva, with an outer 'majora' set and an inner 'minora' set — what are they called?
Labia are the major externally visible structures of the vulva. In other mammals, the labia majora are not present and the labia minora are instead referred to as the labia vulvae.

The second woman to earn a physics doctorate from the University of Vienna, this Austrian-Swedish scientist became the first female full physics professor in Germany — and was instrumental in discovering nuclear fission. Who is she?
Lise Meitner (7 November 1878 - 27 October 1968) was an Austrian and Swedish nuclear physicist who was instrumental in the discovery of nuclear fission.

Made by every living organism and responsible for much of the sour taste in fruit, this dicarboxylic food additive's salt form also serves as a key intermediate in the cell's central metabolic energy cycle — what compound is it?
Malic acid is an organic compound with the molecular formula HO2CCH(OH)CH2CO2H.

This mammal family, uniting skunks and stink badgers, is defined by highly developed scent glands used to ward off predators, and was only split from the weasel family in the 1990s — what family is it?
Mephitidae is a family of mammals comprising the skunks and stink badgers.
This unique group of mammals is the only one whose members lay eggs rather than bear live young, comprising the platypus and four echidna species — what group is it?
Monotreme are mammals of the order Monotremata.

First arising in wormlike creatures some 550 million years ago, this body-wide network coordinates actions and relays sensory signals through a central half and a peripheral half — what system is being described?
Nervous system is the highly complex part of an animal that coordinates its actions and sensory information by transmitting signals to and from different parts of its body.
Beginning in the embryo and maturing a primary oocyte into a fertilization-ready egg cell, what is this reproductive process called?
Oogenesis is the differentiation of the ovum (egg cell) into a cell competent to further develop when fertilized.
Native to the islands of Southeast Asia, this bushy perennial herb in the mint family is prized for a fragrant essential oil used widely in perfumery — what plant is it?
Patchouli (also spelled patchouly or pachouli; Pogostemon cablin) is a species of flowering plant in the family Lamiaceae, commonly called the mint or deadnettle family.

First described in 1850, this family of over 2,000 araneomorph spiders includes the cellar spider and the "vibrating spider" — and lends the nickname "daddy long-legs" to one of its species; what is the family?
Pholcidae are a family of araneomorph spiders. The family, first described by Carl Ludwig Koch in 1850, is divided into 94 genera.
Native to Southeast Asia and a natural, non-hybrid ancestor of both the grapefruit and the bitter orange, this largest of all citrus fruits also goes by the name 'shaddock' — what is it?
Pomelo (PUM-; or pummelo, Citrus maxima), also known as a shaddock, is the largest citrus fruit.
This opening at the center of the iris lets light reach the retina and appears black — round in people, a slit in cats, and even a ring shape in some catfish — what's it called?
Pupil is a hole located in the center of the iris of the eye that allows light to strike the retina.
Named from Greek words for 'rose' and 'tree,' this genus of over 1,000 woody flowering plant species serves as the national flower of Nepal and the state flower of Washington — what is it?

Rhododendron (pl.: rhododendra), from Ancient Greek (rhdon), meaning "rose", and (dndron), meaning "tree", is a very large genus of about 1,024 species of woody plants in the heath family (Ericaceae).
The FAO/WHO Codex standard recognizes 21 species under this common name for small silvery forage fish, distinguished from their larger 'pilchard' cousins mainly by size — what fish is it?
Sardine are common names for various species of small, oily forage fish in the herring suborder Clupeoidei.

Developed by the Chukchi people in the Russian Far East for pulling sleds and companionship, this medium-sized Spitz-family dog breed is smaller than the similar-looking Alaskan Malamute — name the breed?
Siberian Husky is a breed of medium-sized working sled dog.
The largest order of reptiles, this group is set apart by movable quadrate bones that let snakes gape their jaws around oversized prey — what's the order called?
Squamata (Latin squamatus, 'scaly, having scales') is the largest order of reptiles; most members of which are commonly known as lizards, with the group also including snakes.

This medical term describes a resting heart rate above 100 beats per minute in adults, which can be either a normal exercise response or a sign of an electrical problem in the heart — what's the condition called?
Tachycardia is a heart rate that exceeds the normal resting rate.
This viral brain infection, transmitted through the bite of infected parasitic arachnids, saw its European case count climb almost 400% over three decades. What is this arachnid-spread illness?
Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) is a viral infectious disease involving the central nervous system, transmitted by the bite of several species of infected ticks.
With 92 protons and half-lives stretching up to 4.5 billion years, this radioactive metal is handy for dating the age of the Earth — which silvery-grey element?
Uranium is a chemical element; it has symbol U and atomic number 92.
His 1925 Umdeutung paper reinterpreted old quantum theory, and two years later he published a famous uncertainty principle — which German physicist was he?

Werner Heisenberg (5 December 1901 - 1 February 1976) was a German theoretical physicist, one of the main pioneers of the theory of quantum mechanics and a principal scientist in the German nuclear program during World War II.
Launched in 1981 as a joint venture between French and Italian aerospace firms, this high-wing turboprop airliner later formed the basis for a stretched successor introduced in 1989 — which aircraft?
This mushroom genus of more than 400 species includes both the common button mushroom and the field mushroom, the two most-cultivated fungi in the West — which genus is it?
Approved for medical use in the US in 1966, this xanthine oxidase inhibitor lowers uric acid to prevent gout and certain kidney stones — what medication is it?
Allopurinol: Medication. Allopurinol is a medication used to decrease high blood uric acid levels.

Found along the Andes and Pacific coasts of South America, this enormous New World vulture is one of the largest flying birds by wingspan, with males sporting a fleshy comb atop a bald red head — which species is it?
Andean condor: Species of bird. The Andean condor (Vultur gryphus) is a South American New World vulture and is the only extant member of the genus Vultur.
First described by Linnaeus in 1753, this Old World vegetable — better known on dinner plates as celery — is also cultivated for a bulbous root form called celeriac. What is its scientific name?
From the Greek for 'lack of order,' this neurological sign involves loss of voluntary muscle coordination, often linked to cerebellum dysfunction — what is it called?
Ataxia: Neurological impairment of voluntary muscle movement.
A tender herb of the mint family native from Central Africa to Southeast Asia, its Genovese or 'sweet' variety is a kitchen staple worldwide — what is it?
Basil: Culinary herb. Basil (Ocimum basilicum), also called great basil, is a culinary herb of the family Lamiaceae (mints).

Closely related to the beech-oak family and including species widespread across the Northern Hemisphere's temperate and boreal zones, which thin-leaved deciduous hardwood genus is prized for its versatile wood?
Birch: Genus of flowering plants in the family Betulaceae.
Holding the title of smallest great ape, this creature has pinker lips and a darker face than its close cousin, and was once dismissed as merely a 'pygmy' subspecies of it — what is it?
Bonobo: Species of great ape. Taxonomically, members of the chimpanzee/bonobo subtribe Panina—composed entirely by the genus Pan—are collectively termed panins.
Nicknamed 'the lawyer' and 'freshwater cod,' this coldwater fish is the only member of its genus and the sole freshwater species in its entire order — what fish is it?
Burbot: Species of fish. The species is closely related to marine fish such as the common ling and cusk, all of which belong to the family Lotidae (rocklings).
Also known as Flinders rose, this perennial shrub with rounded fleshy leaves and white-to-pink flowers is native across circum-Mediterranean countries — what's the plant called?
Marketed as a COX-2 inhibitor, this NSAID treats arthritis pain and menstrual cramps but carries heart attack and stroke risk warnings — which drug?
The only member of the onion genus native to both the New World and Old World, this perennial herb has edible leaves and flowers and doubles as a natural insect repellent — what is it?
Chives: Species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.

First discovered as an atypical antipsychotic, this medication is reserved for schizophrenia patients who haven't responded to two other drugs, and is also used for psychosis linked to Parkinson's disease — what is it?
Clozapine: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Clozapine, sold under the brand name Clozaril among others, is a psychiatric medication and was the first atypical antipsychotic to be discovered.
Named after a Quechua word meaning the same thing, this New World vulture — with Andean and Californian species — is the largest flying land bird in the Western Hemisphere. What is it?
Condor: Name for two species of vultures.
Commonly called comb jellies, these are the largest animals that swim using rows of cilia, drifting through every ocean as masses of two-layered jelly — what's the phylum?
Ctenophora: Phylum of gelatinous marine animals.
From muntjac to moose, members of the family Cervidae shed and regrow bony skull extensions each year — antlers used to battle rivals. What hoofed ruminant is this?
Deer: Family of hoofed mammals. A deer (pl.: deer) or true deer is a hoofed ruminant ungulate of the family Cervidae (informally the deer family).

He didn't just arrange the known elements — he left gaps and boldly predicted the properties of three undiscovered ones, later vindicated by germanium, gallium, and scandium. Which Russian chemist was he?
Having studied mathematics under Karl Weierstrass, which philosopher founded the school of phenomenology and argued that transcendental consciousness sets the limits of all possible knowledge?
Coiled to just 6 to 7 centimetres but stretching nearly 20 feet if unraveled, this tube connects each testicle to the vas deferens and stores maturing sperm — what is it?

Epididymis: Tube that connects a testicle to a vas deferens. The epididymis serves as an interconnection between the multiple efferent ducts at the rear of a testicle (proximally), and the vas deferens (distally).
The most widely distributed member of its subfamily, this semiaquatic, fish-eating mustelid ranges across Europe, much of Asia, and North Africa's Maghreb — which animal?
Made by nearly every living organism, this protein locks iron away in a safe, soluble form inside cells, and its blood level is the standard test doctors use for anemia or iron overload — what is it?
Ferritin: Iron-carrying protein. Ferritin is a universal intracellular and extracellular protein that stores iron and releases it in a controlled fashion.
As commander of Apollo 8, he led the first crew to circle the Moon and earned the Congressional Space Medal of Honor — who is he?
Frank Borman: American astronaut and lunar explorer (1928–2023)
Pioneered by Gregor Mendel's 19th-century pea plant experiments in Brno, this branch of biology studies heredity and trait inheritance — what is it?
Genetics: Science of genes, heredity and variation.

Weighing up to 175 grams, this South American tarantula is the world's most massive spider — despite a name inspired by an 18th-century engraving of one eating a hummingbird, it rarely actually preys on birds. Which species?
Goliath birdeater: Species of tarantula from South America.
A lentivirus and member of the retrovirus family, it gradually cripples the human immune system — and untreated, leaves roughly 9 to 11 years before the immune collapse called AIDS. What is it?
HIV: Human retrovirus, cause of AIDS. Without treatment, the average survival time after infection with HIV is estimated to be 9 to 11 years, depending on the HIV subtype.

This 19th-century American economist argued in his bestseller 'Progress and Poverty' that a single tax on land values could build a fairer, more productive society — sparking a movement named for him. Who was he?
An American aviator and aerospace engineer who first made his name as a big-budget Hollywood producer, this man grew famous late in life for his reclusive, eccentric ways — who was the magnate?
Howard Hughes: American aviator, aerospace engineer and business magnate (1905–1976)
This 14th-century Arab scholar wrote his most famous work, the Muqaddimah, in just six months and once met the conqueror Tamerlane — who is he?
Ibn Khaldun: Arab Islamic scholar, historian and philosopher (1332–1406)
Sold under the brand name Accutane, this vitamin A-related retinoid treats severe cystic acne but commonly causes dry lips, dry skin, and increased sunburn risk — what is it called?
Isotretinoin: Medication primarily used to treat severe acne.
In a landmark 1913 Columbia University address, this American psychologist championed behaviorism and later became known for the unsettling 'Little Albert' experiment — who is he?
In this eye disorder, the cornea gradually thins and bulges into a cone shape, causing blurry or double vision often linked to excessive eye rubbing as a risk factor — which condition?
Keratoconus: Medical condition involving the eye.
Described both as a science and as the art of justice, this set of enforced rules can be made by legislatures, executive decrees or judges' precedent — what is it?
Sold under the brand name Vyvanse, this prodrug of dextroamphetamine treats ADHD and moderate-to-severe binge eating disorder, taking effect within about 90 minutes — which medication?
Lisdexamfetamine: Central nervous system stimulant prodrug.

Fired by IBM in 1968 for revealing her intent to transition — an apology that took until 2020 — this computer scientist had already invented dynamic instruction handling behind modern out-of-order execution. Who was she?
Lynn Conway: American computer scientist and electrical engineer (1938–2024)
The second woman ever to win the Nobel Prize in Physics (after Marie Curie) shared the 1963 award for her discoveries about nuclear shell structure — who was she?

Encompassing conditions marked by a clinically significant disturbance in thinking, emotional regulation, or behavior that causes real distress or impaired functioning, this broad psychiatric category has causes that remain often unclear — what is the umbrella term for it?
This twin-engine Soviet fighter, known to NATO as 'Fulcrum,' was built in the 1970s to counter American jets like the F-15 and F-16 — which aircraft is it?
Mikoyan MiG-29: Soviet twin-engine jet fighter aircraft. The Mikoyan MiG-29 (Russian: Микоян МиГ-29; NATO reporting name: Fulcrum) is a twin-engine fighter aircraft designed in the Soviet Union.
This telecommunications method encodes text as standardised sequences of just two different signal durations. What are they called?
Morse code is a telecommunications method which encodes text characters as standardized sequences of two different signal durations, called dots and dashes, or dits and dahs.

The males of this stocky Arctic cetacean sport a spiralled 'tusk' up to three metres long — actually a protruding left canine tooth thought to work as a weapon, a tool, and maybe a salinity sensor. What animal is it?

Usually made from unleavened dough that's rolled, cut, or extruded into long strips, this staple food is called pasta in Italian cuisine and split into wheat-based and starch-based varieties in Chinese cooking — what is it?
Noodle: Staple food made from unleavened dough, commonly long and thin.
Discovered by naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace in 1859, this fungus hijacks carpenter ants' brains and marches them down to the forest floor before killing them — which organism?

Ophiocordyceps unilateralis: Species of fungus. Ophiocordyceps unilateralis, commonly known as zombie-ant fungus, is an insect-pathogenic fungus, discovered by the British naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace in 1859.
First domesticated in Mesoamerica and led in production today by India, this tropical fruit belongs to the small genus Carica — what is it?
Papaya: Species of tropical fruit plant.
This inflammation of the sac surrounding the heart causes sharp chest pain that eases when sitting up and worsens when lying down or breathing deeply — what condition is it?
Pericarditis: Inflammation of the pericardium. Pericarditis (PER-i-kar-DYE-tis) is inflammation of the pericardium, the fibrous sac surrounding the heart.
Boasting the longest cones of any spruce and widely planted as a Christmas tree, this European conifer was also the first gymnosperm to have its genome sequenced — which species?
Picea abies: Species of plant. Picea abies, the Norway spruce, Norway fir or European spruce, is a species of spruce native to Northern, Central and Eastern Europe.
Born Joseph Ratzinger, this head of the Catholic Church made history in 2013 by resigning the role, then adopted the title 'emeritus' until his death — who was he?
Pope Benedict XVI: Head of the Catholic Church from 2005 to 2013.

With 348 known species spanning an opportunistic human pathogen, a plant disease-causer, and a soil-dwelling growth-promoter, which gram-negative bacterial genus in Gammaproteobacteria is renowned for its metabolic diversity?
Pseudomonas: Genus of Gram-negative bacteria. Pseudomonas is a genus of gram-negative bacteria belonging to the family Pseudomonadaceae in the class Gammaproteobacteria.
This Norwegian shared the very first Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics, and we owe him the words 'econometrics,' 'microeconomics,' and 'macroeconomics' — who was he?
Ragnar Frisch: Norwegian economist and Nobel Laureate (1895–1973)
Native to Europe, northwestern Africa, and southwestern Asia, this flowering shrub's edible fruit stars in desserts and preserves — what's its species name, better known as the gooseberry?
Ribes uva-crispa: Species of flowering plant in the family Grossulariaceae.
Introduced in the 1970s, this database language let programmers grab many records with one single command, eliminating the need to specify an index path to reach each one — what is it?

Originally from the Mediterranean, this yellowish-gray arthropod has up to 15 pairs of long legs and preys on insects with venom too mild to harm humans — what species commonly invades homes worldwide?
Scutigera coleoptrata: Species of arthropod. Scutigera coleoptrata, also known as the house centipede, is a species of centipede that is typically yellowish-gray and has up to 15 pairs of long legs.
Better known by the brand name Viagra, this drug treats erectile dysfunction and pulmonary arterial hypertension, kicking in within about twenty minutes — what is it?

Sildenafil: Drug for erectile dysfunction and hypertension. Sildenafil, sold under the brand name Viagra among others, is a medication used to treat erectile dysfunction and pulmonary arterial hypertension.
Native to East Asia and the world's most-grown legume, this crop becomes everything from edamame and tofu to soy sauce, nattō and tempeh — what is it?
Soybean: Legume grown for its edible bean.
Named from Greek words for 'twisted' and 'grain,' this genus of spherical bacteria divides along a single axis to form chains, unlike its grape-cluster-forming cousins — coined in 1877, what is it?
Streptococcus: Genus of bacteria. In 1984, many bacteria formerly grouped in the genus Streptococcus were separated out into the genera Enterococcus and Lactococcus.
The lone species in its genus, this African-born leguminous tree gives pods of sweet-tangy pulp used in cuisines worldwide, plus a seed oil and even a dye — what is it?
Tamarind: Leguminous tree bearing edible fruit.

Comprising two Einstein-authored physics frameworks published in 1905 and 1915 — one covering phenomena without gravity, the other explaining gravitation itself — this pair introduced four-dimensional spacetime and superseded Newtonian mechanics. Which pair of physics frameworks is this?
Theory of relativity: Two interrelated physics theories by Albert Einstein.
This shelled reptile retracts its head and neck straight back into its shell for protection, with the largest species growing over a metre long and weighing more than 100 kilograms — what is it?
Named from the Greek word for cheese after being first isolated from casein in 1846, this amino acid carries the one-letter code Y — what is it?
Tyrosine: Amino acid. L-Tyrosine or tyrosine (symbol Tyr or Y) or 4-hydroxyphenylalanine is one of the 20 standard amino acids that are used by cells to synthesize proteins.
Native to southwestern Europe, this venomous viper is also called the asp or aspic viper, with about 4% of untreated bites proving fatal — which snake?
Vipera aspis: Species of snake. Its common names include asp, asp viper, European asp, and aspic viper, among others.

By measuring weak natural radioactivity with sensitive Geiger counters, this American chemist developed a dating method in 1949 that revolutionized archaeology — and won him a 1960 Nobel Prize. Who was he?
Known on the street as a date-rape drug but used medically to treat narcolepsy and cataplexy, this natural neurotransmitter is also a precursor to GABA in the brain — what compound is it?

Γ-Hydroxybutyric acid: Chemical compound. γ-Hydroxybutyric acid, also known as gamma-hydroxybutyric acid, GHB, or 4-hydroxybutanoic acid, is a naturally occurring neurotransmitter and a depressant drug.
Berkelium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for berkelium is Bk. Berkelium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bk and atomic number 97.
